deep.reconstruction:
This folio contains no mathematical derivation. It is a series of separate natural-philosophical and psychological fragments, which the scribe divides with '((Lücke))'. It continues the 'Naturphilosophie' draft from fol. 44.

(A) Continuing the sentence from p. 44: the actions of ponderable matter on ponderable matter are of two kinds. The first is inverse-square attraction and repulsion. The second is light and radiant heat. Both can be explained by one assumption: a homogeneous substance (an aether) fills all of infinite space uniformly, and each particle of it acts only on its immediate surroundings. This is a contiguous-action, continuum hypothesis that rejects action at a distance.

The mathematical law of this action (the 'expression of the force') can be split into two parts:
1. The resistance with which a particle of the substance opposes a change of volume.
2. The resistance with which a physical line element opposes a change of length.

In modern terms (my gloss, not on the page), this is an elastic-continuum energy with two terms. The first is a dilatational (bulk) term depending on the volume change det(1+grad u) - 1 ≈ div u. The second depends on how lengths of line elements change, ds'^2 - ds^2 = 2 e_ij dx_i dx_j, where e is the strain tensor; it is effectively the deviatoric or shear part. Riemann assigns gravitation and electrostatics to the volume term. He assigns propagation of light and heat and electrodynamic/magnetic action to the line-element term. This matches the companion fragment 'Gravitation und Licht' printed in Weber's edition of the Werke. There gravitation comes from the aether streaming into ponderable matter (cf. p. 44, 'einströmt und dort verschwindet'). A steady, incompressible radial inflow into a sink gives velocity proportional to 1/r^2, which is the inverse-square law (my gloss).

(B) Epistemological remark: Newton's distinction between laws of motion ('axioms') and hypotheses is untenable. The law of inertia is itself a hypothesis: if a single material point existed alone in the world and moved with a given velocity, it would keep that velocity forever. The point is that the law is a counterfactual idealization and cannot be verified empirically.

(C) Fechner quotation (from Zend-Avesta): 'When the body of the lower soul dies, the higher soul takes it from its life of perception into its life of memory.' Riemann infers that on Fechner's view the souls of dead creatures are the elements of the earth-soul's mental life.

(D) §1: Different thought-processes differ mainly in their temporal rhythm (time scale). If plants have souls, their hours and days correspond to our seconds. The corresponding unit for the earth-soul's outward activity may span many millennia. So within recorded human history, all motions of the inorganic crust can still be explained mechanically. This is a qualitative scaling argument with no mathematics.

(E) Start of a psychological passage, continued on p. 46. The elements of mental life are the simplest distinguishable items of inner perception: simple sensory presentations, e.g. that of a red point. Each is the mental expression of a bodily process bounded in space and time. The next page specifies these bounds: the peripheral end of a primitive nerve fibre, and about 1/9 to 1/10 of a second.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no computation. The claim that light propagation and electrodynamics rest solely on resistance to length change, and gravitation and electrostatics solely on resistance to volume change, is a speculative physical hypothesis. It is not consistent with later physics (Maxwell/Einstein), but it is not a slip.
The plant/earth-soul time-scale argument is speculative, Fechnerian natural philosophy rather than a derivation.

results.what: Aether filling all space, acting only by contiguity; the law of action split into a resistance to volume change (gravitation, electrostatics) and a resistance to length change of line elements (light, heat, electrodynamics/magnetism)
results.modern_name: Elastic-solid / continuum aether theory (bulk vs. shear or line-element strain energy); field theory by contiguous action
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy, Green (1830s-40s), MacCullagh (1839), later Kelvin and Maxwell; the gravitational inflow (sink) aether also appears in Challis and Bjerknes

results.what: Newton's laws of motion (e.g. inertia) are hypotheses, not axioms; the law of inertia is a counterfactual about a lone body
results.modern_name: Critique of the epistemic status of the law of inertia (precursor to the Neumann/Mach discussions)

results.what: Mental processes distinguished by characteristic time scale; plant and earth-soul time units vastly longer than human ones
results.modern_name: Relativity of the subjective time scale ('Moment') of organisms

results.what: Simple sensory presentation as the mental expression of a spatially and temporally bounded nerve process
results.modern_name: Psychophysical parallelism / elementary sensation (Herbartian simple presentation)

deep.surprise_reason: This is material from Riemann's natural-philosophy fragments: the aether with volume and line-element resistances, the critique of Newton's axioms, and the Fechner discussion. Essentially the same text was printed by Weber and Dedekind in the Werke ('Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', 'Gravitation und Licht', 'Erkenntnisstheoretisches', 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik'), so it is known. At most, minor textual variants (e.g. the time-scale remark) are of interest.

checkable.asserts: A steady radial inflow with speed 1/r^2 is divergence-free away from the sink: an incompressible aether flowing into a point mass gives an inverse-square field (gloss on the inflow hypothesis).
The potential 1/r is harmonic away from the origin, giving the inverse-square force.
Volume change under principal stretches equals the trace (dilatation) to first order. This separates the 'volume change' part from the line-element 'length change' part of the strain.

transcription_corrections: Margin at the first gap: 'Seite 10' is more likely 'bis zu 10' (cf. 'bis zu 4' on p. 46 and the '10 ×' on p. 44), an editorial marker.
'durch ihren zeitlichen Rhythmus[?]': the manuscript appears to read 'Rythmus' (period spelling), i.e. rhythm.
'Die verschiedenen Denkprozesse[?]': probably 'Denkprocesse' in Riemann's spelling.
The '§ 1' before 'Die verschiedenen' looks more like a bracketed '[1]' or a crossed mark than a section sign.

The pencil margin notes at the Fechner passage and near the bottom ('Vorzugsweise[?]') are uncertain and probably editorial (e.g. 'Vorzugsweise' or a reference to Fechner). They are not part of Riemann's text.
